name: P4 Behavioral Model (BMv2)
what_it_is: BMv2 is the second version of the reference P4 software switch, written in C++17, that interprets JSON files generated by P4 compilers to implement packet-processing pipelines. It is designed as a development and testing tool, not a production-grade switch.
components: simple_switch — primary v1model target for P4_16 programs
simple_switch_grpc — gRPC-enabled variant with dynamic module loading
l2_switch — example target with SimplePre multicast engine
simple_router — example target with SimplePreLAG multicast engine
runtime_CLI.py — CLI for table population and multicast programming
p4dbg.py — debugger tool for runtime packet-level inspection
nanomsg client — real-time event message consumption
measurement: Event logger via nanomsg: broadcasts table hits/misses and parser transitions
Nanomsg client: real-time event message consumption
configuration: --nanolog: enable event logging via nanomsg IPC
--load-modules: dynamically load shared objects at runtime
-i port@interface: bind switch port to network interface
CMake build-time flags: toggle nanomsg, Thrift, PI, pdfixed, debugger, coverage, module loading, stress tests, logging macros, P4_16 stack support
constraints: Not production-grade: significantly lower throughput and latency than hardware switches
PSA architecture support is tentative and not fully mature
No auto-generated per-program code (design decision; limits runtime efficiency)
Variable-length fields beyond 32 bits only recently added
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml found in the repository
No full P4_14 feature parity (direct registers missing)
